crossRefs.note: “If you meet your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, you shall surely bring it back to him again.
If you see the donkey of him who hates you fallen down under his burden, don’t leave him. You shall surely help him…
But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who…
But he, desiring to justify himself, asked Jesus, “Who is my neighbor?”
Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
I will most gladly spend and be spent for your souls. If I love you more abundantly, am I loved the less?
Brothers, even if a man is caught in some fault, you who are spiritual must restore such a one in a spirit of…
Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
We exhort you, brothers: Admonish the disorderly; encourage the faint-hearted; support the weak; be patient toward all.
Therefore lift up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees,
and make straight paths for your feet, so what is lame may not be dislocated, but rather be healed.

translations.web: You shall not see your brother’s donkey or his ox fallen down by the way, and hide yourself from them. You shall surely help him to lift them up again.
translations.bsb: If you see your brother’s donkey or ox fallen on the road, you must not ignore it; you must help him lift it up.
translations.kjv: Thou shalt not see thy brother's ass or his ox fall down by the way, and hide thyself from them: thou shalt surely help him to lift them up again.
translations.asv: Thou shalt not see thy brother's ass or his ox fallen down by the way, and hide thyself from them: thou shalt surely help him to lift them up again.
